items.text: Procurement exception case PR-2026-0488 was resolved by R. Menon regarding a request for ₹85,000 for indirect MRO calibrated bore gauges from vendor V-023. The standard vendor check failed because the ISO/IEC 17025 calibration certificate had expired 3 days prior to the request. The standard process did not fit because blocking the vendor would have cut off the only local supplier of calibrated gauges, and the certificate lapse was purely administrative. R. Menon approved step codes REQUEST_RENEWED_CERT, KEEP_VENDOR_ACTIVE, and HOLD_PO. The outcome was that the renewed certificate was received in 5 days and the purchase order was released. The lesson learned is that a recently expired certificate should be treated as a hold rather than a rejection when the vendor is in good standing. | When: Thursday, April 02, 2026 | Involving: R. Menon (Procurement Ops), vendor V-023 (supplier of calibrated bore gauges) | The user requested an extraction of how procurement exceptions at Kaveri were resolved, specifically focusing on the failed standard check, the reason the standard process was insufficient, the approved step codes, the outcome, and the lesson learned for case PR-2026-0488.

items.text: When a vendor in good standing has a recently expired ISO 9001 or ISO/IEC 17025 certificate, the procurement process should trigger a hold rather than an automatic rejection. The approved procedure involves applying step codes REQUEST_RENEWED_CERT, KEEP_VENDOR_ACTIVE, and HOLD_PO to allow for certificate renewal while maintaining the vendor relationship. This lesson is supported by cases PR-2026-0417 involving vendor V-017 and PR-2026-0488 involving vendor V-023.

The lesson learned is that a recently expired certificate should be treated as a hold rather than a rejection when the vendor is otherwise in good standing. | When: Saturday, March 14, 2026 | Involving: Procurement Ops team | To improve future procurement exception handling and prevent unnecessary vendor rejections.

items.text: When a primary approver is on leave and the request amount is within the delegate's limit, the procurement process should use step code ROUTE_DELEGATE to route the request to a delegate approver to avoid delays, as demonstrated in case PR-2026-0301.

Procurement exception resolution for case PR-2026-0301 involving a request for ₹1,10,000 for indirect MRO spindle bearings from vendor V-008 for cost centre CC-MACH. The standard 'approver' check failed because the primary approver E-104 was on leave until March 13, 2026. The standard process did not fit because the request would have been delayed for eight days. The human reviewer R. Menon approved the step code ROUTE_DELEGATE, allowing delegate E-112 to approve the request on the same day. The lesson learned is that when an approver is away and the amount is within the delegate's limit, the request should be routed to the delegate. | When: Thursday, March 5, 2026 | Involving: R. Menon (Procurement Ops reviewer), E-104 (primary approver on leave), E-112 (delegate approver), V-008 (vendor) | The user requested an extraction of how procurement exceptions at Kaveri were resolved, specifically focusing on failed checks, process fit, approved step codes, outcomes, and lessons learned for case PR-2026-0301.

items.text: When a vendor changes their bank account details, the standard 'bank' check is insufficient to prevent payment fraud; the required procedure is to execute step codes VERIFY_BANK_CALLBACK, HOLD_PAYMENT, and HOLD_PO. This protocol was established following case PR-2026-0233, where a recent account change necessitated a callback to a known number and a payment hold before the purchase order could be released.

The lesson learned is that a recent bank change requires a callback on a known number and a payment hold before any other actions are taken. | When: Friday, February 20, 2026 | Involving: Procurement Ops team | To establish a standard protocol for preventing payment fraud when vendor banking details are modified.

The callback to the number on file confirmed the new account, and the Purchase Order (PO) was released after 2 days. | When: Friday, February 20, 2026 | Involving: R. Menon | The verification process successfully validated the vendor's account change, allowing the procurement to proceed.

R. Menon approved step codes VERIFY_BANK_CALLBACK, HOLD_PAYMENT, and HOLD_PO to resolve the exception. | When: Friday, February 20, 2026 | Involving: R. Menon (Procurement Ops) | These steps were necessary to mitigate the risk of payment fraud identified by the bank account change.
